mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not negative (< 0%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which depresses earnings for industrial firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 1% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation above 3% for two consecutive months signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and inflation, which increases real discount rates and erodes real corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in housing starts (HOUST) above the previous year's peak by more than 15% in a single month signals an unsustainable housing boom, which historically precedes corrections in equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises > 15% above previous year's peak in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) in the same month indicates a statistical artifact or data inconsistency, but if interpreted as a labor market normalization after a shock, it may precede a short-lived equity rally, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises AND UNRATE rises in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> 0%) in at least 60% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% for six consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue and profit forecasts, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered periods.
